steps.name: 13-firing-limits
steps.limits:
The moved beacon has a negative discriminant at the configured speed. The comparison leaves its request unserved and draws no invented projectile flight. More aiming precision cannot make this request reachable.
A valid ballistic solution need not be a safe route. The chosen low arc can hit a wall, while the high arc can meet an overhead obstacle. Both need collision checks in a game world.
The beacon is stationary. Motion during the longer flight can invalidate a high arc that was correct at launch; a moving-target solver must predict the encounter rather than aim at an old position.
The calculation assumes constant gravity, no drag and an instantaneous choice of muzzle direction. It does not include turret turn limits, wind, projectile size or an intervening collision. This example accepts only targets ahead of the launcher and at or above the water.
